prerequisites: Level B1 of English (Common European Framework) is required to attend the course in a profitable way.

learning_outcomes.text: Students acquire a good knowledge about the structure of Contemporary Standard English and important cultural aspects of interlinguistics communication.
They apply this knowledge both in receptive and productive writing and speaking skills, appropriate for their upper-intermediate level.
They can analyze and evaluate language structures.
By the end of the course, students should have acquired a good understanding of the structure of contemporary standard English and of the cultural aspects relevant to cross-linguistic communication.
By the end of the course, students should be able to analyse and evaluate linguistic structures.
By the end of the course, students should be able to apply this knowledge to their receptive and productive skills in writing and conversation, in line with their intermediate-advanced level.

syllabus_topics: Review of English language functions and grammar structures
Introduction of main lexical and structural elements of English for Engineering
Present tenses: present simple, present continuous, past perfect
Past tenses: past simple and past continuous
Future tenses: will, be going to and present continuous
Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous
B2 Grammar points: Conditionals (If...will / If...would); (if clauses)
B2 Grammar points: How to express the concept of habit with 'used to'
Lexical morphology: Expressions of quantity and quality
Differences between formal and informal language
Lexical contents/Semantic areas: Sports and hobbies
Lexical contents/Semantic areas: Lifestyles - home & family
Lexical contents/Semantic areas: Science and Technology
Lexical contents/Semantic areas: Business and Employment
Vocabulary, with specific activities to strengthen technical vocabulary in each Module
Grammar to consolidate the most common morphosyntactic structures in the technical language
Skills, through texts and activities to develop Listening, Speaking and Writing skills
Morphological and lexical structures through the study of "grammar in discourse" and "English in use"
teaching_methods: Narrative text reading and work with other linguistic input

assessment_methods.method: Writing/reading test assessing functional, structural and lexical knowledge/skills and ability to understand a technical or scientific text.
Written test assessing functional, structural and lexical knowledge/skills applied to the description of graphs or process diagrams, and ability to understand a technical or scientific text.

assessment_rules: The final test is assessed as Passed or Failed. The assessment includes a writing/reading test aimed at assessing functional, structural and lexical knowledge/skills, and the ability to understand a technical or scientific text. For some groups, the written test specifically assesses these skills applied to the description of graphs or process diagrams.
bibliography: Grammar and Vocabulary for First and First for Schools Book with Answers, Cambridge University Press
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Industriale (Industrial Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
